edits.match: It starts to work within hours, is taken twice a day with or without food, and its one important harm is bleeding, so people carry an anticoagulant alert card and tell every dentist and surgeon they see.
edits.replacement: It starts to work within hours, is taken twice a day with or without food, and its main harm is bleeding, so people carry an anticoagulant alert card and tell every dentist and surgeon they see.
edits.reason: UNSAFE: 'its one important harm' is an overstated absolute (anaemia, nausea, rash and rare liver injury are also recognised); softened to the NHS framing that bleeding is the most common/main harm.

notes: Line-by-line check. The domain-restricted search surfaced NHS trust/ICB material rather than the nhs.uk medicines pages; excerpts support bleeding more easily (nosebleeds, heavier periods, bleeding gums, bruising) as the most common effect, NSAIDs/aspirin to be flagged, herbal products interacting, rare liver test changes. 'Twice a day with or without food' is standard labelling (general knowledge, no dose figure). 'Stop 24-72 hours before surgery', 'do not double up', 'intracranial about half the rate of warfarin' and the reversal-agent note all predate the patch. Boxed warning on stopping in AF and spinal haematoma are MedlinePlus Important Warning content (general knowledge). No protected field changed.
